content.thinking: Dark screen with the title "קרן כספית", which is what I came for. The page calls it a low-risk fund like treasury bills and bank deposits, but it promises no guaranteed return, and I can't make sense of the small "123 מקור 123 חושב 123 הזנה" line.
מסכי ההסבר של הקרן הנזילה מציגים תשואה יומית של 3.25% מול 1.8% לפיקדון, לפי לאומי ולפני מס ועלויות. עוד לא הבנתי את חישוב המס, אז אדלג עליו, ואני עובר למסך הבא.

Screen 4 gives the expected return as after management fees, before tax, not guaranteed, and says the money-market fund and bank deposit carry no holding fee. I'm checking screen 5 next, since the cost breakdown is the part I need.

I read six screens of the fund's terms and stopped there, since the black background was straining my eyes. The risk section says there is no state guarantee and no insurance, the value can fall, and redemptions can be suspended for several trading days in exceptional cases.

input.answer: I didn't decide anything. A money-market fund (קרן כספית) seems to pay more than my deposit (3.25% against 1.8% for a year) and I can take the money out any trading day. But it says nothing is guaranteed, the value can go down, there's no state guarantee or insurance, and I couldn't find how much it actually costs. So I'll ask you, and the clerk at the bank, before I move anything.
